title: Control flow introduction
recap: A program normally executes statements one after another, but control flow statements let the execution path branch. A conditional statement runs its associated statement only when a condition holds, and a loop repeats a statement while a condition holds.

In this lesson you meet the simplest branch: an if statement with an else. Choosing between exactly two outcomes from one fixed comparison is the foundation every later control flow structure builds on.
objectives: Follow one execution path through a small deterministic program.
Branch on a fixed comparison and print a different result per branch.
Exercise both branches with fixed calls, without reading input.
warnings: Only one branch of an if/else runs on each call.
Do not replace the two calls with hard-coded report lines.
Keep the comparison in the condition; do not print both results.
challenge: Complete printScoreResult so a score at or above passMark prints pass after the shared prefix, and a lower score prints fail. Keep both calls in main so the same function exercises both branches in one deterministic run.
hints: The shared prefix std::cout << "Score " << score << ": "; stays outside the if statement.
Use if (score >= passMark) for the passing branch and an else for the failing branch.
Print only the word pass or fail inside each branch, newline included.
